games.key_factors: Squiggle weighted consensus: PTA by 6.4 (24/28 models). CRITICAL Rule 15: Holy Grail (82%) tips RIC by 1.2 and What Snoo (79%) tips RIC by 11.6 — the TOP TWO accuracy-weighted models DISAGREE with consensus. Rule 15 triggered: reduce consensus by 30%+. Base: PTA by 6.4. Reduction: 6.4 × 0.7 = PTA by 4.5. Rule 14 (bounce-back): RIC lost by 60 last week (qualifies for +5 to +8pt bounce). However, checking: RIC's trajectory is 71→60→43 (declining each week). Context note says regression effect may be exhausted if team didn't bounce after first big loss. RIC lost R1 by 18, then lost R2 by 42, then lost R3 by 60 — they never bounced. BUT Rule 14 says 'NEVER assume declining trajectories continue indefinitely.' After a 60pt loss, apply minimum +5pt bounce. Adjusted: PTA by 4.5 minus 5pt bounce = RIC by 0.5. Footy Forecaster AGREES with top Squiggle models: tips RIC by 5 (54.4%). Wheelo tips PTA by 7.8 (58.9%). Wheelo is the outlier here. PTA ODELO at MCG: net -56.4 (TERRIBLE — PF lift -21.7, PA lift +34.7). But only 4 games and weighted heavily to 2024-25 — LOW-MEDIUM reliability. PTA without Rozee (hamstring, TBC — elite midfielder) is significant. Soldo OUT (knee, season) hurts ruck. RIC without Nankervis (hamstring, 5-7wks) and Lynch (hamstring, 3-4wks) — both long-term, already in form stats. MCG HGA +3.3 for RIC. PTA travel -1.5pts (654km short). RIC 7-day break vs PTA 6-day break. RIC's Tim Taranto (SC 119.3) is their only premium performer. PTA's Zak Butters (SC 118.3) is elite. Weather: 18.8C, dry, 7km/h wind — no impact. H2H last 10: PTA leads 7-3 dominantly. Balancing all factors: top 2 Squiggle models and FF favour RIC, Wheelo and simple consensus favour PTA. PTA's superior talent should prevail but by much less than consensus suggests. Predicting PTA narrowly.

Perth Stadium HGA +11.3pts is the strongest in the comp — WCE ODELO at Perth shows +13.9 net lift (PF lift +8.2, PA lift -5.7 — HIGH reliability, 25 games). SYD ODELO at Perth shows net +35.7 but only 3 games (MEDIUM reliability) — and those were likely 2024-25 SYD which was a different team. SYD travel: cross-country 3291km = -10pts (includes -2pts body clock to Perth). HOWEVER, SYD is coming off a BYE (+3pts preparation advantage) with 16 days rest vs WCE's 6 days rest — massive 10-day rest differential. SYD's bye offsets some travel penalty. Net SYD travel/rest impact: -10 + 3 (bye) + 2 (rest advantage) = -5pts net penalty. WCE form: 2-1, upset PTA last week by 2pts at Perth (ODELO venue lift confirmed). WCE attack -8.8 (Wheelo) is weak but Perth lifts it. SYD 2-1, lost to HAW by 17 last game but that was R2 (16 days ago). SYD attack +1.6, defence +6.2 (Wheelo). SYD's Charlie Curnow and Brodie Grundy (SC 112.0) provide forward/ruck strength. SYD's I50 efficiency 41.1 scores/I50 is mediocre. Rule 18: SYD scored 142 in R1 (blowout vs ESS) — without that: (93+83)/2 = 88 baseline, not 106. Blend: ~97. WCE scored 92 in R3 upset — their best game. Model lesson 13: when ODELO venue offensive lift >+5.0 AND opponent has venue offensive penalty >-3.0, home underdog is live. WCE lift +8.2 qualifies. SYD at Perth has PF lift +7.4 (not a penalty). So Rule 13 doesn't fully trigger. Weather: 21.5C, dry, 17km/h wind SW — moderate wind could affect kicking at Perth, slight scoring reduction. Final model: SYD superior team but Perth fortress + travel penalties narrow the gap significantly. Wheelo/FF margin of ~16 more realistic than Squiggle's 23.4.
